questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) With the help of examples, distinguish between a Direct and an Indirect tax.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Direct tax.** A tax that is levied **directly on the income or wealth of the person** who is meant to pay it, so that the burden cannot be passed on to somebody else. It is paid straight to the government by the taxpayer. Examples: personal income tax, company (profit) tax, capital gains tax and tax on property or wealth.

**Indirect tax.** A tax levied on **goods and services (expenditure)**. It is collected by the seller or importer, who is the person legally charged, but it is generally **passed on** to the consumer in the price. Examples: value added tax (VAT), excise duties on beer, tobacco and fuel, and customs duties on imports.

| Basis | Direct tax | Indirect tax |
|---|---|---|
| Levied on | Income and wealth | Goods and services |
| Who bears the burden | The person taxed (cannot be shifted) | Usually shifted to the consumer |
| Effect on the poor | Can be progressive | Tends to be regressive |
| Examples | Income tax, company tax | VAT, excise, customs duties |

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Distinguish between a Tax incidence and an Impact of a tax.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Impact of a tax.** The point at which the tax is **first imposed**: it is the person or firm **legally responsible** for paying the tax to the government.

**Incidence of a tax.** The **final resting place** of the tax: it is the person who **finally bears the burden**, after the tax has been shifted by changes in prices.

**Example.** The government places an excise tax on beer. The impact is on the brewery, which pays the tax to the government. The brewery raises the price of beer, so that most of the burden is passed on to the consumers; the incidence is therefore mostly on the consumers (and partly on the brewery if it absorbs some of the tax). When a tax cannot be shifted, as with income tax, the impact and the incidence fall on the same person.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Explain Four (4) advantages of a indirect tax.

(10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** An indirect tax is a tax on spending (goods and services). Its advantages are the following.

1. **Wide coverage and large revenue.** Everyone who buys taxed goods pays, including people in the informal sector whose incomes are difficult to measure and to tax directly. A wide base gives the government a large and regular revenue.

2. **Convenient and difficult to evade.** The tax is collected by the seller at the point of sale or by customs at the border and is included in the price, so that the consumer cannot easily avoid it, and the cost of collection is low.

3. **It can discourage the consumption of harmful goods.** Heavy taxes on alcohol, tobacco and similar demerit goods raise their price and reduce consumption, and protect health.

4. **It is flexible.** The government can change rates quickly to meet its needs, to control demand or to correct the balance of payments, and can exempt basic necessities (for example, essential foodstuffs and medicines) to protect the poor.

5. **It can protect local industries.** Import duties raise the price of foreign goods and help infant industries.

6. **It is less painful and it is voluntary.** The tax is paid in small amounts hidden in the price, so people complain less, and a person can reduce the tax paid by buying less of the taxed goods.

(Any four, each explained.)

**Conclusion.** Indirect taxes are an easy and productive source of revenue, and are also a tool for influencing consumption.
